items.q: Years of broken promises have gradually ______ public confidence in the government's climate pledges.
items.vi: Nhiều năm thất hứa đã dần dần bào mòn niềm tin của công chúng vào những cam kết khí hậu của chính phủ.
items.explanation: Word choice: gradually + an object (public confidence) needs a transitive verb meaning wear away slowly, so eroded fits (erode confidence/trust/support). ✗ collapsed — intransitive, fall down suddenly; cannot take confidence as its object; ✗ dissolved — melt into liquid or end a partnership/parliament, not a feeling; ✗ decayed — intransitive, rot or decline; takes no object.

items.q: By the end of this decade, the logistics firm ______ its entire delivery fleet with electric vehicles.
items.vi: Đến cuối thập kỷ này, công ty logistics sẽ thay thế xong toàn bộ đội xe giao hàng bằng xe điện.
items.explanation: Tense: By the end of this decade is a future deadline, and the action will be finished before it, so the future perfect will have replaced is needed. ✗ will replace — simple future only predicts the action; it does not show completion before the deadline; ✗ has replaced — present perfect links past to now, not to a future point; ✗ will be replacing — future continuous shows the work still in progress then.

items.q: I hate to ______, but the grant you have been promised is far from guaranteed.
items.vi: Tôi không muốn làm bạn mất hứng, nhưng khoản tài trợ mà bạn được hứa hẹn còn lâu mới chắc chắn.
items.explanation: Idiom: the speaker apologises (I hate to) before giving disappointing news that spoils a hope, so rain on your parade = spoil someone's excitement. ✗ throw in the towel — give up a fight; ✗ bite the bullet — face something painful bravely; ✗ jump the gun — act before the proper time. None describes bringing bad news.

items.q: Rising sea levels ______ a grave threat to low-lying island nations such as the Maldives.
items.vi: Mực nước biển dâng gây ra mối đe dọa nghiêm trọng cho các quốc đảo thấp như Maldives.
items.explanation: Collocation: the verb that goes with a grave threat (also a risk, a danger, a problem) is pose, meaning present or cause. ✗ put — put someone at risk / under threat, but never put a threat; ✗ place — place someone in danger, again not with threat as object; ✗ set — set a record, a target, a trap, not a threat.

items.q: The documentary ______ fresh anger over the dumping of toxic waste near the village.
items.vi: Bộ phim tài liệu đã khơi dậy làn sóng phẫn nộ mới về việc đổ chất thải độc hại gần ngôi làng.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: the object fresh anger over a scandal needs a verb meaning provoke strong feelings, so stirred up (stir up anger/trouble/controversy). ✗ brought up — mention a topic or raise a child; ✗ took up — start a hobby, or occupy time/space; ✗ set up — establish a company or arrange equipment. Only stir up collocates with anger.

items.q: The samples ______ contaminated in the laboratory; they were sealed the moment they were collected.
items.vi: Các mẫu không thể nào bị nhiễm bẩn trong phòng thí nghiệm được; chúng đã được niêm phong ngay lúc thu thập.
items.explanation: Modal deduction: the second clause (sealed the moment they were collected) proves contamination was impossible, and a confident past deduction of impossibility is can't have been. ✗ mustn't have been — must is used for positive deduction only; its negative is not used for deduction; ✗ needn't have been — it happened but was unnecessary; ✗ shouldn't have been — it happened and was wrong.

items.q: The appeal court ______ the original verdict, rejecting all three grounds of appeal.
items.vi: Tòa phúc thẩm giữ nguyên phán quyết ban đầu, bác bỏ cả ba căn cứ kháng cáo.
items.explanation: Word choice: an appeal court that rejects the grounds of appeal confirms the lower court's decision, and the legal verb for that is upheld (uphold a verdict/ruling/conviction). ✗ sustained — in court, a judge sustains an objection, not a verdict; ✗ retained — keep possession of something; ✗ preserved — keep from damage or decay. Neither is a legal confirmation.

items.q: ______ did the new tram line cut journey times across the city, but it also reduced traffic on the ring road by a fifth.
items.vi: Tuyến tàu điện mới không những rút ngắn thời gian đi lại trong thành phố mà còn giảm một phần năm lượng xe cộ trên đường vành đai.
items.explanation: Inversion: the second half but it also reduced completes the pair Not only … but also, and the fronted negative triggers did the tram line cut. ✗ Hardly — pairs with when (Hardly had … when); ✗ Only after — needs a time phrase or clause before the inversion (Only after the line opened did …); ✗ Not until — likewise needs a time expression first.

items.q: Junior staff are often reluctant to ______ by questioning decisions made higher up.
items.vi: Nhân viên cấp dưới thường ngại gây xáo trộn bằng cách chất vấn những quyết định từ cấp trên.
items.explanation: Idiom: questioning decisions made higher up disturbs a settled situation, so rock the boat = upset the status quo. ✗ spill the beans — reveal a secret; ✗ break the ice — ease the awkwardness at a first meeting; ✗ hold the fort — take charge while others are away. Only rock the boat means causing trouble by challenging things.

items.q: The missing funds uncovered so far are only the ______ of the ______; investigators believe far more was diverted.
items.vi: Số tiền thất thoát được phát hiện cho đến nay chỉ là phần nổi của tảng băng chìm; các điều tra viên tin rằng còn nhiều hơn thế đã bị chuyển đi.
items.explanation: Idiom: only the … of the …; far more was diverted means a small visible part of a much larger hidden problem, which is the tip of the iceberg. ✗ top / mountain — literal words, not an idiom for a hidden problem; ✗ edge / cliff — on the edge of a cliff means near disaster, not a small part; ✗ peak / glacier — not an English expression at all.

items.q: The researchers, most of ______ had spent years in the Arctic, warned that the ice was thinning faster than predicted.
items.vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu, mà phần lớn trong số họ đã dành nhiều năm ở Bắc Cực, cảnh báo rằng băng đang mỏng đi nhanh hơn dự đoán.
items.explanation: Relative pronoun: after a quantifier + of in a non-defining clause about people (the researchers, most of ___), the object form whom is required. ✗ which — for things, not people; ✗ them — a personal pronoun cannot join two clauses without and (most of them had would be a run-on); ✗ whose — possessive, must be followed by a noun.

items.q: The report ______ that roughly a third of the region's wells are contaminated with pesticides.
items.vi: Báo cáo ước tính rằng khoảng một phần ba số giếng trong khu vực bị nhiễm thuốc trừ sâu.
items.explanation: Word choice: roughly a third is an approximate figure, and the verb that gives one, followed by a that-clause, is estimates. ✗ assesses — judge the level or importance of something; takes a noun object, not that + figure; ✗ evaluates — judge quality or value; also object only; ✗ appraises — formally value property or performance; same problem.

items.q: The airline ______ a loss of forty million dollars in the final quarter of the year.
items.vi: Hãng hàng không ghi nhận khoản lỗ bốn mươi triệu đô la trong quý cuối năm.
items.explanation: Collocation: in financial reporting a company posts a profit or a loss, meaning it officially announces the result. ✗ noted — observe or write down; a company notes a trend, not its own loss; ✗ marked — mark an anniversary or a change, not a financial result; ✗ scored — score goals, points or a success, never a loss.

items.q: The auditor recommended that the foundation ______ an independent trustee before the next funding round.
items.vi: Kiểm toán viên khuyến nghị quỹ bổ nhiệm một ủy viên quản trị độc lập trước vòng tài trợ tiếp theo.
items.explanation: Subjunctive: after recommended that (also suggest, insist, demand), the that-clause verb is the bare base form for any subject: the foundation appoint. ✗ appoints — ordinary present with -s; wrong after a recommendation verb; ✗ appointed — past tense; the appointment has not happened yet; ✗ would appoint — would is not used in this pattern (British English allows should appoint, never would).

items.q: By unveiling its own electric van a day early, the rival firm ______ at the trade fair.
items.vi: Bằng cách ra mắt chiếc xe tải điện của mình sớm một ngày, hãng đối thủ đã cướp mất sự chú ý của công ty tại hội chợ thương mại.
items.explanation: Idiom: unveiling its own van a day early grabbed the attention the company expected at the fair, so stole the company's thunder = take someone's expected praise by acting first. ✗ pulled the company's leg — tease or joke with someone; ✗ twisted the company's arm — pressure someone into doing something; ✗ got the company's goat — annoy someone.

items.q: ______ generous the pension scheme may seem, few employees stay long enough to benefit from it.
items.vi: Dù chương trình hưu trí có vẻ hào phóng đến đâu, ít nhân viên ở lại đủ lâu để được hưởng lợi từ nó.
items.explanation: Concession: the blank is followed directly by an adjective (generous) and then subject + verb (the pension scheme may seem), so However + adjective = no matter how. ✗ Whatever — must be followed by a noun (Whatever its generosity); ✗ No matter — needs how before an adjective (No matter how generous); ✗ Although — introduces a full clause, not a bare adjective.

items.q: Before accepting the overseas posting, she wanted to ______ the decision with her family.
items.vi: Trước khi nhận nhiệm vụ ở nước ngoài, cô ấy muốn bàn bạc kỹ quyết định đó với gia đình.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: the decision with her family before deciding means discuss it fully, so talk over (talk something over with someone). ✗ talk back — reply rudely to authority; takes no object; ✗ talk down — talk down to someone = speak condescendingly, or talk down a price; ✗ talk into — talk someone into doing = persuade; needs a person, not a decision, as object.

items.q: Several studies have ______ a direct link between air pollution and premature births.
items.vi: Nhiều nghiên cứu đã xác lập được mối liên hệ trực tiếp giữa ô nhiễm không khí và sinh non.
items.explanation: Word choice: studies that prove a direct link exists are said to establish it (establish a link/fact/connection). ✗ founded — start an organisation or a city; ✗ instituted — introduce a system, policy or procedure; ✗ formulated — work out a plan, theory or formula in words. None means proving a connection by evidence.

items.q: ______ for the anonymous donation, the hospice would have closed last winter.
items.vi: Nếu không nhờ khoản quyên góp ẩn danh, nhà chăm sóc cuối đời đã phải đóng cửa vào mùa đông năm ngoái.
items.explanation: Conditional: the result would have closed last winter is past and unreal, so the condition must be third-conditional, inverted: Had it not been for. ✗ Were it not — second conditional; present or future unreal, clashing with last winter; ✗ If it were not — same present meaning; ✗ Unless it were — unless does not combine with for + noun in this pattern.

items.q: ______ how little rain has fallen this year, the region's reservoirs are in surprisingly good shape.
items.vi: Xét đến việc năm nay mưa quá ít, các hồ chứa của khu vực đang ở trong tình trạng tốt đến bất ngờ.
items.explanation: Participle: how little rain has fallen is a fact taken into account, and Considering (how / that / + noun) is a fixed form meaning in view of, needing no subject of its own. ✗ Considered — passive, would mean the reservoirs are being considered; ✗ To consider — an infinitive of purpose; reservoirs cannot consider; ✗ Having considered — needs a thinking subject, not reservoirs.

items.q: Figures released by the lobby group should be ______, since it is funded by the very industry it defends.
options: taken with a pinch of salt
items.answer: taken with a pinch of salt
items.vi: Những số liệu do nhóm vận động hành lang công bố nên được tiếp nhận một cách dè dặt, vì nhóm này được tài trợ bởi chính ngành mà nó bênh vực.
items.explanation: Idiom: figures from a group funded by the very industry it defends should be doubted, so taken with a pinch of salt = not believed entirely. ✗ swept under the carpet — hide a problem from view; ✗ kept under wraps — keep something secret; ✗ put on the back burner — postpone until later. Only pinch of salt is about believing a claim.

items.q: After a decade in banking, she has finally got used ______ far less than her former colleagues.
items.vi: Sau một thập kỷ làm trong ngành ngân hàng, cuối cùng cô ấy đã quen với việc kiếm được ít hơn nhiều so với các đồng nghiệp cũ.
items.explanation: Gerund after preposition: in get used to, the to is a preposition, so it takes the -ing form: get used to earning. ✗ to earn — bare infinitive belongs to used to + verb (past habit), a different structure with no get; ✗ earning — drops the required to; ✗ for earning — used takes to, not for.

items.q: The foundation has agreed to ______ on the running costs of the shelter ______ the council pays for the repairs.
items.vi: Quỹ đã đồng ý gánh vác chi phí vận hành của nhà tạm trú với điều kiện hội đồng thành phố chi trả cho việc sửa chữa.
items.explanation: Double blank: agreed to ___ on the running costs means accept a burden, so take on; the council paying is the condition, so provided (that). ✗ put / unless — put on = wear or gain weight; unless = except if, the wrong logic; ✗ bring / in case — bring on = cause; in case = as a precaution; ✗ carry / whereas — carry on = continue; whereas = contrast, not condition.

items.q: The retraining scheme ______ of three phases, the first of which begins next spring.
items.vi: Chương trình đào tạo lại gồm ba giai đoạn, giai đoạn đầu tiên bắt đầu vào mùa xuân tới.
items.explanation: Word choice: the blank is followed by of, and the only verb that takes of in this meaning is consists: the scheme consists of three phases. ✗ comprises — takes a direct object with no preposition (comprises three phases); ✗ composes — works the other way round: three phases compose the scheme; ✗ constitutes — likewise the parts constitute the whole, and no of.

items.q: Small manufacturers often struggle to ______ the strict new emissions standards.
items.vi: Các nhà sản xuất nhỏ thường chật vật để đáp ứng các tiêu chuẩn khí thải nghiêm ngặt mới.
items.explanation: Collocation: the verb for satisfying standards (also requirements, targets, deadlines) is meet. ✗ reach — reach a level, a goal or an agreement; a standard is satisfied, not arrived at; ✗ fill — fill a gap, a post or an order, never a standard; ✗ match — be equal to something; matching a standard is not the phrase for complying with it.
